findings.question: Q4
findings.title: R14-C-F2 is still open, though README section 9 marks it fixed. The entries listed just before a read-back (`before`) are thrown away unless an unread state is already recorded, so a spend state that rolls back in place during its own read-back is dropped and the executed action can be admitted and dispatched again
findings.evidence: owners.py:607 lists `before = self._entries(key)` for every handed account. On a successful read-back, `before` and `after` feed only `_seen_entries` (owners.py:740-743) and `_against_unread` (owners.py:744). `_against_unread` returns None straight away when no unread state is recorded (owners.py:674-676). So a read state whose `before` held a spend entry that `after` and the read history lack is accepted: `_seen` takes the read history (owners.py:739) and the listed spend is never recorded. On the not-read-back path, `_read_back` discards `before` and `_unread` lists the container again after the failed attempts (owners.py:613-618 -> 621-626). The recorded entries are therefore the container after any in-place rollback during those attempts, and if they are a prefix of `_seen_entries`, `_note_unread` records nothing (owners.py:656-659). The docstring at owners.py:590-591 says the entries are those held 'just before the read-back', and README:194-195 / owners.py:405 say 'held then'; neither is what the unread path records. README:625-626 lists 'Fixed, MINOR: R14-C-F2 / F14-F2 (a read state is checked against unread entries listed just before AND just after its read-back)', but R14-C-F2's own reproduction (review_r14_result.json, lens C) had no unread state ('diverged: [] unread: {}'). The round-14 control tests/mind/test_authority_review_r14.py:136-158 covers only the variant where the spend was first made unread by an earlier verification, which is F14-F2's case. The mutants list 'the after-read listing ignored' (README:399) but no mutant or control for R14-C-F2's no-unread case.
findings.reproduction: Static reading only; nothing was executed. Path 1 (R14-C-F2's recipe unchanged): on the battery fixture with BudgetReader.following(lambda: (dict(o.ledgers), dict(o.experiments))), the executor settles run.1 with a detail whose __str__, on the next verification's first read-back attempt, runs object.__setattr__(led, 'charges', s0.charges + (other.1,)) and raises the interpreter's 'changed size during iteration'. Attempt 2 reads S0+other.1. before=(spent, run.1) and after=(spent, other.1); no unread state is recorded, so owners.py:675-676 returns None, the record is accepted, and a fresh project_world + gateway.admit + dispatch of simulate_pulse runs the executor a second time. Path 2 (unread path): the same rollback goes to the observed tuple `earlier` (identical objects), and the account's to_dict override keeps raising the mutation error on all three attempts. `_unread` lists `earlier`, which `_seen_entries` extends, so nothing is recorded. After the override is removed, gateway.dispatch(admitted) re-admits on a history equal to `_seen` and the executor runs twice.
findings.why: The handed state (spent, run.1) was observed (its entry objects were listed), and the reader still decides on a state that does not begin with them. That contradicts README:226-228 ('a return to an earlier state never re-authorizes what such a state had moved past') and 196-199. The trigger bypasses the owner's BudgetHistoryViolation guard (object.__setattr__) or mutates the private _evaluations list, so under the trust-boundary rule it stays MINOR, as round 14 rated it. It is still a genuine correctness defect of the forward-only follower, so it keeps Q4 PARTIAL. The report's 'Fixed' disposition matters for the gate: it would let a later round treat Q4 as clean while the finding's own reproduction still holds.
findings.fix: Require stable listed history matching read-back length; preserve pre-read entries on unread/rollback

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: New in 7b4a0de8: an honest account that moved forward in place past a recorded unread state during a concurrent read-back is refused for good with the false reason 'rewrote the entries', contrary to README:240-241
findings.evidence: owners.py:681-686: a read state is cleared only if BOTH `before` and `after` extend the unread entries U, and is 'behind unread' only if U extends BOTH. Any other case goes to `_rewrote_unread`, and owners.py:748-750 records it in `_diverged` (for good). When before is a strict prefix of U and U is a strict prefix of after (all the same objects, an append-only move), neither test holds, so the account is refused for good with the text at owners.py:690-692 ('rewrote the entries of a state ... no longer begins with exactly those entry objects'), which is false. At 1c9fdd84 only `before` was compared (review_r14_result.json R14-C-F2 evidence: '`before` is used only to compare against a previously recorded unread state'), and this case was 'behind' (refused only while behind). README:240-241 says 'Concurrent verifications never refuse for good an account that only moved forward in place and that its owner reads back.' U is listed AFTER the other verification's failed attempts (owners.py:614, 621-622), so it can fall strictly between a concurrent verification's two listings. README section 8 (lines 497-513) documents honest torn read-backs of a large experiment that is extended every 0.1 s while one read-back takes about 0.45 s.
findings.reproduction: Static reading only; nothing was executed. Use a BOUND experiment extended in place at about 0.1 s intervals with a read-back of about 0.45 s. V1's three attempts tear (not read back) and `_unread` lists U with n+2 entries; it holds new entries, so it is recorded, and V1 compares. Meanwhile V2 listed before (n entries), succeeded on one attempt, and listed after (n+4 entries); it compares after V1. owners.py:681 fails (before is shorter than U), owners.py:684 fails (after is longer than U), and owners.py:686 + 748-750 refuse the account for good. Every later admission that binds it is refused until a new reader is built.
findings.why: A follower that refuses an honest forward-only account for good, saying it rewrote its history, asserts a false fact about the owner's account (a refusal reason that misstates why). It contradicts a stated guarantee and is a regression introduced by the round-14 change. It fails closed (no wrong admission), so it is MINOR, but it is a semantic defect of the budget follower and adds to Q4 PARTIAL.
findings.fix: Moving read-back is transient; record its entry prefix instead of declaring a rewrite

findings.title: New in 7b4a0de8: the seal fires on ANY BaseException raised while a handing is parsed, including the caller's own stack exhaustion or an asynchronous KeyboardInterrupt. It retires every account of the reader for good with the reason 'not a pair of account dicts'

A RecursionError from a deep caller stack (the round-12 b1203 window, documented as 'the caller's own stack exhausted inside the reader'), a MemoryError, or an operator's Ctrl-C arriving inside `_handed` seals an honestly handed pair of dicts. README:208-209 says 'a verification's own deep call stack never refuses an honest account for good'. README:159-161 and owners.py:381-383 describe the seal as applying to 'a handing that is not a pair of dicts'. At 13051154 only the TypeError from `_items` was converted (CRIT14-1 evidence).
findings.reproduction: Static reading only; nothing was executed. findings.why: This is a fail-closed availability regression, and the refusal reason misstates why ('not a pair of account dicts' for a stack or interrupt condition). It contradicts the README's claim about deep stacks. MINOR, but a semantic defect of the budget follower (Q4).

Code at 95f3869e (src/engcore/mind/world/owners.py):

- The seal is set at lines 874-882, with the text 'this reader refuses every account from then on'.

Refutation angles I tried:
(a) Is this just the accepted residual 'a spend and its rollback both between two verifications look like no change'? restore_only shows that residual yields the same outcome when nobody was handed S1. Here a verification WAS handed S1 and the reader explicitly sealed for that reason. Rounds 13-14 (R14-A-F1 et al., CRIT14-1) treated a handed-but-not-read-back state as one that must not be re-authorized. The noseal control proves the same interleaving is refused when S1 is handed as dicts. The MappingProxyType path is therefore strictly weaker than the dict path, which is exactly CRIT14-1's regression class.
(b) Is it the residual 'a verification whose accounts() ... hands no pair of mappings'? A MappingProxyType pair is a pair of mappings, and CRIT14-1 was confirmed MAJOR for exactly that handing.
(c) Is it the residual 'one that leaves ... between being handed accounts and comparing them, which only the verifications then waiting for it refuse'? That residual names its causes in parentheses: the caller's stack exhausted inside the reader, or an interrupt outside the read-back. The seal is a different exit. Round 14's disposition claims 'refuse every account from then on', not 'only waiters refuse'.
(d) Is V1's decision legitimately 'before' the seal? V1 compares and decides after the seal, on a state that rolls back what the sealing handing may hold, so 'from then on' is violated.

findings.evidence: owners.py:607-610 lists `before` and `after` around _account, but nothing relates them to `history`. owners.py:681-683: _against_unread clears the unread record when `before` and `after` begin with it, whatever `history` holds. owners.py:740-743: _seen_entries is set from `after` even when len(history) != len(after). owners.py:736-739: with no unread record, a read state whose `before` holds an entry absent from `history` is accepted. The README line 197-199 claim ('its container begins with exactly those entry objects ... it moved on in place, and from then on its history decides') holds for the container but not for the history decided on.
findings.reproduction: ~/br11-review/r15/B-architecture/p2_unread_cleared_by_lying_readback.py: the spend's detail raises the interpreter's mutation error, so it is not read back and the unread record is set (`unread recorded: True`). Then the live ledger's to_dict is overridden on the instance, either (lie) returning the pre-spend dict or (aba) rolling charges back with object.__setattr__, serializing, and re-applying them. In both, the container still holds the spend (`2 > 1`). Output: `[lie] same authorization dispatched again: True; executor calls 2; unread now []` and `[aba] ... True; executor calls 2`. ~/br11-review/r15/B-architecture/p2b_before_listing_dropped.py: a readable spend rolled back in place inside the next verification's read-back, with no unread record: `[rollback_in_readback] same authorization dispatched again: True; executor calls 2`.
findings.why: The new check is meant to order a read state against an unread state. Because it never ties the decided history to the listed entries, the observation it rests on (entry identity) and the record it decides on (the serialized text) can disagree. It is a genuine correctness gap in the round-14 rule, and it bears on Q4. Rated MINOR because every trigger needs execution-side tampering with its own owner object: an instance to_dict override, or object.__setattr__ past BudgetLedger's settle-only guard. That is the same technique and rating as round 14's R14-C-F2 control, and no honest concurrent schedule produces it (honest moves only append).
findings.fix: Require stable listed history matching read-back length; preserve pre-read entries on unread/rollback

findings.title: A KeyboardInterrupt raised by the content of any handed account, even one no world binds, makes every verification of every account raise KeyboardInterrupt forever. The account is never refused, and every admission and dispatch is aborted. This contradicts README:244 ('An account no verification reads ... refuses nothing').

Nothing ever moves that account to _diverged. Probe ~/br11-review/r15/critic/kbi_content.py hands an extra unbound ledger 'side.ledger' whose second charge's detail __str__ raises KeyboardInterrupt. Four successive reads of the bound solver ledger each printed 'KeyboardInterrupt escaped the read of an UNRELATED account: from content', and at the end 'diverged: [] unread: {('ledger', 'side.ledger'): 2}'. authorize_dispatch catches only (WorldRefused, ScientificCoreError, AttributeError, TypeError, KeyError, ValueError) (admission.py:421), so the interrupt reaches the Mind's caller.
